source.title: Towards Universality: Studying Mechanistic Similarity Across Language Model Architectures
source.authors: Junxuan Wang; Xu-Yang Ge; Wentao Shu; Qiong Tang; Yunhua Zhou; Zheng-Fu He; Xi-Peng Qiu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: It tests induction-circuit behavior in a different architecture using path patching, a causal method, and compares the identified Mamba circuit with the Transformer circuit. This bears on architectural transfer, but does not test the proposed training-time phase change.
record.gate_note: The paper reports path-patching results on an induction-pattern task in Mamba. It does not measure training dynamics, loss-versus-token-index in-context learning, few-shot task learning, or formation across checkpoints. The cited Transformer findings are background, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: Path patching on Mamba-130M finds an induction circuit for [A][B]…[A]→[B], structurally analogous to the Transformer one. This is a result on V4's claim that induction behaviour appears in other architectures. It is a new setting (a non-attention architecture) rather than a different method on the original question, so T3 rather than T2. Nothing on formation, training dynamics, loss by token index or few-shot tasks is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Mamba and Transformers implement structurally analogous induction circuits, with a Mamba-specific off-by-one motif from the local convolution. They also conclude that most SAE features are similar across the two architectures. They acknowledge the circuit comparison is qualitative.
record.recipe_differences: Uses repeated-token induction inputs and studies the circuit with path patching in Mamba; it does not reproduce the original training-time loss and head-formation measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Path-patching effects vary by layer and token position: layer 17 has the largest reported state effect, layer 20 a weaker one, and the SSM input at B1+1 has a much larger effect than at A1 or B1. Results are also reported across distances 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features in Pythia-160M and Mamba-130M (and RWKV-169M) are highly correlated across architectures. Mean MPPC is 0.74 for Mamba and 0.65 for RWKV, against a 0.76 seed-variant skyline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational (SAE feature) universality across language-model architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Off-by-one convolution motif also appears in Mamba on the IOI task (Appendix H).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mamba writes token information into the SSM state at the following position across tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), as stated in the supplied metadata; the paper text is marked Preprint. Under Review.
record.problems: The induction-circuit comparison is qualitative and limited to one Mamba model; the authors state that they have not quantitatively measured circuit similarity. The reported path-patching means have no uncertainty estimates. The study does not test training-time formation or the broader sizes and runs in V4.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix G, Table 1 reports patching at layers other than 17 and 20 across the listed distances; these cells were omitted to stay within the row cap, since the text says other layers are mostly irrelevant. Appendix G, Tables 2–4 are represented for the key B1+1, A1, and B1 positions across distances.

untested.parts: No small attention-only transformers and no previous-token/induction-head composition analysis; the Transformer circuit is cited background.
No training checkpoints, formation window, loss bump or in-context learning time course.
No loss-by-token-index measure and no share of in-context learning attributed to induction.
Only one Mamba model (130M) and one training run. No sizes, seeds or modalities. RWKV is tested only for SAE feature similarity, not for induction. Clean-run induction accuracy is not reported.
No variation of data or training setup.

missing.what: Patching x at B1+1 with [A][B']…[A] corruption: near-zero values (0.26, 0.24, −0.06, 0.27, −0.11) contrasting with B1.
Patching the SSM input at B1+2 and B1+3: near-zero contrasts.

record.verdict_notes: Paper is a preprint under review. The 128 synthetic induction samples per condition have no uncertainty reported. The Transformer induction circuit is drawn from Olsson et al., not re-measured here. Layer-20 and contrast-position rows localise components and should not be read as evidence of weaker induction.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test small attention-only Transformers or whether their induction heads form by composing with a previous-token head.
No training-time formation window, loss bump, or time course of in-context learning is measured.
No large-transformer in-context-learning loss-by-token-index measure or estimate of the share carried by induction heads.

The study investigates one Mamba model at 130M and reports an RWKV feature-similarity experiment, not an induction-circuit test. It does not test multiple sizes, training runs, modalities, or whether induction heads specifically occur in every architecture.
No comparison of data or training setups for induction-circuit formation or persistence of in-context learning.
No few-shot task-learning test separating induction copying from other heads or mechanisms.
No training trajectory or analysis of whether induction formation comprises several transitions.

relationships.reason: Patching the layer-17 SSM state (r1–r5), the SSM input at B1+1 (r11–r15), and x at B1 (r26–r30) and at A1 (r31–r35) each drops B's logit by about 8–17, at every distance tested. This shows an induction circuit in a non-attention architecture.
relationships.display_finding: Patching the layer-17 state, state-space input after B1, or inputs at B1 and A1 lowers B's logit by about 8–17 across all tested distances.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Sections 6.1–6.2 and Appendix G show an induction circuit involving local convolution and layer-17 SSM state, with substantial patching effects at every tested distance.

relationships.reason: Induction is carried by a local convolution plus the SSM state, not by heads. Information enters the state one token late, at B1+1 rather than B1 (r11–r15 vs r21–r25; Section 6.3). So 'heads' must be read as an analogous circuit in this architecture.
relationships.display_finding: Local convolution and state-space memory implement induction, with information entering the state one token after B1.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The literal heads wording needs qualification: Mamba implements induction through convolution and recurrent state, with a delayed write at B1+1. This qualifies the mechanism's description, not the presence of induction.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: The literal heads wording needs qualification: Mamba implements induction through convolution and recurrent state, with a delayed write at B1+1. This qualifies the mechanism's description, not the presence of induction.

relation.reason: The study's own causal patching results bear directly on induction universality across architectures.

tranche.reason: Path patching identifies induction circuitry in a new architectural setting, Mamba, without reproducing the original training-time measurements.

source_check.notes: Appendix G uses 128 randomly generated induction examples per condition; circuit similarity is assessed qualitatively. Section 6.3 says B1, but the abstract, Section 6.1 and Table 2 establish the delayed write at B1+1.

statements.correction: Preprint under review; review venue unspecified in the study text. Mamba-130M, Pile-trained; Appendix G, Tables 1–2 confirm all cited logit changes.
statements.problem: All Mamba results match, but the supplied study text does not identify ICLR as its review venue.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Patching the layer-17 state and the SSM input at B1+1 strongly changes B’s logit, while patching other positions can have little effect; the authors describe the resulting circuit as structurally analogous to the Transformer induction circuit (r1–r5, r11–r25).
